The decomposition audit of revision 1 accepted the split, the five frozen child types and the proofs of four children. It rejected one item: density_monotonicity's derivation of the monotonicity identity (M), which used the wrong sign for the mean-curvature term. As the audit required, every key, lean_name, lean_statement and depends_on is byte-identical to revision 1. Corrections in density_monotonicity (Simon Ch. 4, 3.3-3.6 and 4.1-4.8, derived directly for the contract's varifold):
(1) Radial identity. The contract's convention is that the integral of div_M X dmu equals minus the integral of X.H dmu. For X = phi_eps(|x-y|/t)(x-y) this gives n I - t I' + t J' = -C. Setting a = t^-n I and E = t^-(n+1) C, that is a' = t^-n J' + E, so the curvature pairing enters with a plus sign. The book's 4.1 prints a minus sign. SimonGMT's cutoffMass_deriv_identity has the same corrected form.
(2) Cancellation. Put F_0 = -E/(1+a) and F = exp(integral_0^t F_0) = exp(-integral_0^t E/(1+a)). Then (F(1+a))' = F t^-n J' exactly. Hoelder gives |F_0| <= g with integral_0^t g = (Lambda/4)(t/R)^(1-n/p), using kappa = (p-n)/(4p).
(3) Passage to closed balls, now proved. Tonelli on Lebesgue measure on [s,r] times mu restricted to B_R(y), with a Borel version of the integrand, together with the support of d_t phi_eps(rho/t) in (rho/(1+eps), rho), gives the squeeze e^(-(1+eps)Lambda/4) A_eps <= Phi_eps(r) - Phi_eps(s) <= e^((1+eps)Lambda/4)(1+eps)^n A_eps. Dominated convergence then gives:
- I_eps -> mu(B_t(y)) and C_eps -> C;
- F_eps -> F;
- A_eps -> the integral over the closed-ball annulus B_r(y) minus B_s(y), because phi_eps = 1 on (-infinity, 1].
Hence e^(-Lambda/4) A <= Phi(r) - Phi(s) <= e^(Lambda/4) A for 0 < s < r < R.
(4) No bridge to the library varifold. The proof uses only the contract's fields, HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature, the sibling tangent_plane_ae and Mathlib. SimonGMT's corrected Chapter04 lemmas are cited only as a cross-check.
(5) The lower bound (ii) no longer needs upper semicontinuity. At good points z near y, the weighted tangent plane gives liminf t^-n mu(B_t(z)) >= omega_n theta(z) >= omega_n. Continuity from above on closed balls then transfers the bound to y.
(6) Explicit constants: delta_0 = min{kappa/8, kappa omega_n/8, 1/(24n)} and C_0 = 2e/kappa. They give (13/7) omega_n <= 2 omega_n in (i) and (49/64) omega_n >= omega_n/2 in (ii). Both bounds were also checked numerically.

subproblems.title: A.e. weighted approximate tangent planes and measurability of tangentProj (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2-1.9)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U an open subset of R^(n+l), and V = v(M, theta) a RectifiableVarifold n l U: M ⊆ U is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, theta > 0 on M, theta is a.e. measurable for H^n restricted to M, and the integral of theta over M ∩ K is finite for every compact K ⊆ U. Let mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density theta and p_x = V.tangentProj x. Then (a) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (b) for mu-a.e. x there is a linear subspace T of R^(n+l) which is an approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T, which includes dim T = n), and p_x = T.starProjection is the orthogonal projection onto T.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n V.carrier V.mult x T ∧ V.tangentProj x = T.starProjection
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (only-if part), Remark 1.3, Theorem 1.6 (=>), Remarks 1.8(1),(2) and Theorem 1.9 (=>); the printed proofs are copied and specialized to the contract's varifold, and the measurability statement is the remark recorded as fact (F1) in the parent proof. This child is the fact (F1) of the parent proof.

Notation. eta_{x,r}(y) := r^-1 (y - x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap); for A ⊆ R^(n+l) and E ⊆ R^(n+l), H^n(eta_{x,r}(A) ∩ E) = r^-n H^n(A ∩ (x + r E)). C_c := compactly supported continuous real functions on R^(n+l). B_r(x) is the closed ball. mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x, which by definition is the orthogonal projection onto the subspace chosen (by choice) among the weighted approximate tangent spaces (Def. 1.7) of M w.r.t. theta at x when one exists, and 0 otherwise.

1. Reduction to H^n-a.e. statements on M. mu is a with-density measure of H^n restricted to M, so mu << H^n restricted to M and mu(R^(n+l) \ M) = 0. Hence a property holding at H^n-a.e. point of M holds mu-a.e., and two maps that agree at H^n-a.e. point of M agree mu-a.e. It therefore suffices to find an H^n-null set Z and a Borel map g from R^(n+l) into the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps of R^(n+l) such that every x in M \ Z has a weighted approximate tangent space T_x with p_x = p_{T_x} = g(x). Then (b) holds mu-a.e., and V.tangentProj = g mu-a.e.; a Borel map into a finite-dimensional normed space is strongly measurable, so (a) follows. We may also replace theta by a Borel function theta~ equal to theta at H^n-a.e. point of M: none of the integrals in Def. 1.7 changes (the exceptional null set stays null under the similarities eta_{x,r}), and for x outside the null set {x in M : theta(x) != theta~(x)} the values theta(x) = theta~(x) agree, so the weighted approximate tangent spaces for theta and theta~ coincide at such x. Below theta denotes this Borel representative on M (still > 0 on M after discarding a further null set).

2. Localization to U. For k >= 1 let W_k := {x in U : |x| < k and dist(x, R^(n+l) \ U) > 1/k} (drop the second condition if U = R^(n+l)). Each W_k is open, its closure is a compact subset of U, and U is the union of the W_k. Put M_k := M ∩ W_k. M_k is H^n-measurable and countably n-rectifiable (a subset of M), and for every compact K ⊆ R^(n+l) the integral of theta over M_k ∩ K is at most the integral of theta over M ∩ closure(W_k), which is finite by the contract hypothesis; so (M_k, theta) satisfies the hypotheses of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7 and Thm. 1.9. If x in W_k, f in C_c with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and 0 < r < dist(x, R^(n+l) \ W_k)/R, then f(eta_{x,r}(z)) = 0 for every z outside W_k, so the integrals over eta_{x,r}(M) and over eta_{x,r}(M_k) of f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) coincide (and are finite) for all small r > 0. Hence an n-dimensional subspace T is a weighted approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M_k at x. Since M is the union of the M_k, it suffices to prove, for each fixed k, that H^n-a.e. x in M_k has a weighted approximate tangent space and to produce the Borel representative on M_k.

3. Lusin (Simon Rem. 1.8(1)). Fix k. Apply Lusin's theorem (Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17) to the finite Borel-regular measure nu_k := theta H^n restricted to M_k and the Borel function theta: for each j there is a compact set K_j ⊆ M_k with nu_k(M_k \ K_j) < 1/j and theta restricted to K_j continuous (no nesting of the K_j is needed); hence nu_k(M_k \ union_j K_j) = 0. Since theta > 0 on M_k, also H^n(M_k \ union_j K_j) = 0. As theta|K_j is continuous and positive on the compact set K_j, c_j := min over K_j of theta > 0, so H^n(K_j) <= c_j^-1 * (integral of theta over K_j) < infinity.

4. Vanishing density of the weight off K_j (Simon Rem. 1.8(1), upper density theorem Ch. 1, 3.6). For each j, nu_k restricted to M_k \ K_j is a finite Borel-regular measure, so by the upper density theorem (Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6), r^-n * (integral of theta over (M_k \ K_j) ∩ B_r(x)) -> 0 as r -> 0 for H^n-a.e. x outside M_k \ K_j, in particular for H^n-a.e. x in K_j. Let E_j be the exceptional H^n-null subset of K_j.

5. C^1 cover (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3; printed proof of the only-if part). By Def. 1.1, M_k ⊆ M_0' ∪ union_m F_m(R^n) with H^n(M_0') = 0 and F_m : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz. By the C^1 approximation theorem (Ch. 2, 1.5, applied to each component) there are C^1 maps G_{im} : R^n -> R^(n+l), i = 1, 2, ..., with L^n({u : F_m(u) != G_{im}(u)}) < 1/i. With Z_m := R^n \ union_i {F_m = G_{im}} we get L^n(Z_m) = 0, hence H^n(F_m(Z_m)) <= (Lip F_m)^n L^n(Z_m) = 0, and F_m(R^n) ⊆ F_m(Z_m) ∪ union_i G_{im}(R^n). By the area formula (Ch. 2), H^n(G_{im}({J G_{im} = 0})) <= integral over {J G_{im} = 0} of J G_{im} dL^n = 0. If J G_{im}(u) != 0, then D G_{im}(u) is injective, and by the inverse function theorem there is eps_u > 0 such that G_{im} is an injective immersion on a neighbourhood of the closed ball B_{eps_u}(u) and a homeomorphism of that neighbourhood onto its image; then N := G_{im}(open ball of radius eps_u about u) is an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold with H^n(N) < infinity, parametrized by the single C^1 map phi := G_{im} restricted to that open ball, which has injective differential and continuous inverse on N. Countably many such balls cover {J G_{im} > 0} (Lindelof). Collecting all null sets into N_0 and enumerating the submanifolds as N_1, N_2, ... with parametrizations phi_i : O_i -> N_i, we get M_k ⊆ N_0 ∪ union_{i >= 1} N_i with H^n(N_0) = 0, each N_i sigma-compact (hence Borel) with H^n(N_i) < infinity. As in Remark 1.3 put K_{j,i} := (K_j ∩ N_i) \ union_{i' < i} N_{i'} for i >= 1: these are Borel, pairwise disjoint, K_{j,i} ⊆ N_i, and H^n(K_j \ union_i K_{j,i}) <= H^n(N_0) = 0.

6. Unweighted tangent planes of K_j (printed proof of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 (=>), applied to the finite-measure set K_j). Fix j, i and f in C_c with spt f ⊆ B_R(0). For x in K_{j,i} and r > 0,
 integral over eta_{x,r}(K_j) of f dH^n = integral over eta_{x,r}(N_i) of f dH^n - integral over eta_{x,r}(N_i \ K_j) of f dH^n + integral over eta_{x,r}(K_j \ N_i) of f dH^n.
Since x in N_i and N_i is a C^1 submanifold, the first term tends to the integral of f over T_x N_i = D phi_i(phi_i^-1(x))(R^n) with respect to H^n as r -> 0 (blow-ups of a C^1 submanifold converge to its tangent plane; area formula for phi_i). The other two terms are bounded in absolute value by sup|f| * r^-n H^n(B_{rR}(x) ∩ (N_i \ K_j)) and sup|f| * r^-n H^n(B_{rR}(x) ∩ (K_j \ N_i)). The measures H^n restricted to N_i \ K_j and to K_j \ N_i are finite and Borel-regular, so by the upper density theorem both bounds tend to 0 for H^n-a.e. x in K_j ∩ N_i (such x lie outside both sets). The exceptional null set E'_{j,i} does not depend on f. Hence for every x in K_{j,i} \ E'_{j,i}, T_x N_i is the approximate tangent space (Def. 1.4) of K_j at x; in particular (Rem. 1.5(3)) r^-n H^n(K_j ∩ B_{rR}(x)) -> omega_n R^n, so r^-n H^n(K_j ∩ B_{rR}(x)) is bounded for all small r.

7. Weighted tangent planes (Simon Rem. 1.8(1)). Let x in K_{j,i} \ (E_j ∪ E'_{j,i}). For f in C_c with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and small r > 0,
 integral over eta_{x,r}(M_k) of f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = theta(x) * (integral over eta_{x,r}(K_j) of f dH^n) + integral over eta_{x,r}(K_j) of f(y) (theta(x + r y) - theta(x)) dH^n(y) + integral over eta_{x,r}(M_k \ K_j) of f(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y).
The first term tends to theta(x) * (integral of f over T_x N_i) by step 6. The second is at most sup|f| * sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in K_j ∩ B_{rR}(x)} * r^-n H^n(K_j ∩ B_{rR}(x)), which tends to 0 by continuity of theta|K_j at x and the boundedness at the end of step 6. The third is at most sup|f| * r^-n * (integral of theta over (M_k \ K_j) ∩ B_{rR}(x)), which tends to 0 because x is not in E_j (step 4). Hence T_x := T_x N_i, an n-dimensional subspace, satisfies Def. 1.7 for (M_k, theta) at x, hence for (M, theta) at x by step 2: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T_x holds. Since H^n(M_k \ union_j K_j) = 0, H^n(K_j \ union_i K_{j,i}) = 0 and all exceptional sets are null, this holds for H^n-a.e. x in M_k, and therefore (step 2) for H^n-a.e. x in M.

8. Identification of p_x. At every such x we have x in M, so theta(x) > 0, and weighted approximate tangent spaces at x are unique (Def. 1.7: 'evidently P_x is unique'; SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, which only needs theta(x) != 0). Therefore the subspace selected by choice in the definition of V.tangentProj is T_x, i.e. p_x = T_x.starProjection. With step 1 this proves (b).

9. Borel representative and measurability. For each piece (k, j, i) define g_{k,j,i}(x) := p_{T_x N_i} for x in N_i. Writing x = phi_i(u) with u = phi_i^-1(x) (continuous on N_i) and A := D phi_i(u) (injective and continuous in u), T_x N_i = A(R^n) and p_{T_x N_i} = A (A^T A)^-1 A^T, which depends continuously on x in N_i; hence g_{k,j,i} is Borel on the Borel set N_i. Enumerate the countably many Borel sets K_{j,i} (over all k, j, i) as B_1, B_2, ... with corresponding maps g_m, let B'_m := B_m \ union_{m' < m} B_{m'}, and define g(x) := g_m(x) for x in B'_m and g(x) := 0 off the union of the B'_m. Then g is Borel. The union of the B_m has H^n-null complement in M (steps 2, 3, 5), and by steps 7-8, for H^n-a.e. x in B'_m ⊆ K_{j,i} we have p_x = p_{T_x N_i} = g(x). Thus p_x = g(x) at H^n-a.e. point of M, so by step 1 V.tangentProj agrees mu-a.e. with the Borel (hence strongly measurable) map g, i.e. V.tangentProj is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. This proves (a). QED
proof_key_steps: Reduce mu-a.e. claims to H^n-a.e. claims on M (mu << H^n restricted to M) and replace theta by a Borel representative
Localize to M_k = M ∩ W_k with closure(W_k) compact in U, so theta is integrable on compacts and blow-ups of M and M_k agree
Lusin: compact K_j ⊆ M_k exhausting M_k up to a null set, theta|K_j continuous and positive, H^n(K_j) < infinity
Lemma 1.2/Remark 1.3: cover by finite-measure embedded C^1 submanifolds N_i up to an H^n-null set; disjoint Borel pieces K_{j,i}
Proof of 1.6 (=>) with the upper density theorem: T_x N_i is the unweighted approximate tangent space of K_j at a.e. x in K_{j,i}
Remark 1.8(1): continuity of theta on K_j and vanishing density of theta H^n on M_k minus K_j give the weighted approximate tangent space T_x N_i

subproblems.title: Density bounds (Simon 5.2.4) and annular monotonicity inequality under 2.3
subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l >= 0 and p > n there are delta_0 in (0, 1/8] and C_0 >= 0, depending only on n, l, p, such that: whenever U is open, V = v(M, theta) is a RectifiableVarifold n l U with generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= delta_0 and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho (Simon 2.3) hold, then, with mu = V.weight, omega_n = unitBallVolume n, closed balls B_s(y) and p_x = V.tangentProj x: (i) mu(B_s(y)) <= 2 omega_n s^n for all y with |y| <= 3 delta rho and all 0 < s <= rho/2; (ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n / 2 for all y in spt V with |y| <= 3 delta rho and all 0 < s <= rho/2; (iii) for all y with |y| <= 3 delta rho and all 0 < s <= r <= rho/2: r^-n mu(B_r(y)) <= e^2 s^-n mu(B_s(y)) + C_0 delta + e^2 * (integral over B_r(y) \ B_s(y) of |(x - y) - p_x(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^(n+2) dmu(x)), where the ball masses are taken as real numbers (toReal) and the integral is the Bochner integral.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's facts (M) and (P) (Simon Ch. 5, 2.4, with explicit constants), specialized to the three estimates used by the Lipschitz graph corollary, and the monotonicity identity of Simon Ch. 4, Section 4 (4.1-4.8), whose cutoff argument and passage eps -> 0 are those of Ch. 4, 3.3-3.6 (the cutoff phi, the squeeze 3.5 and the limit 3.6). Item (iii) is the inequality used in the parent's step 5(b) (book: 2.6 (9)), written for general radii. Two corrections to the printed Ch. 4 text are applied.
(1) The coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 is kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value required by the integration after 4.4 (SimonGMT Chapter04 lpMeanCurvatureKappa).
(2) Under the contract's convention (integral of div_M X dmu = - integral of <X, H> dmu), the radial first-variation identity 4.1 carries the PLUS curvature pairing: with a(t) := t^-n I(t) and E(t) := t^(-n-1) C(t), one has a' = t^-n J' + E, where the book prints a minus sign. Consequently the cancellation factor is F = exp(integral of F_0) with F_0 := -E/(1 + a), i.e. F(t) = exp(- integral_0^t E(u)/(1 + a(u)) du).
The derivation is carried out directly for the contract's RectifiableVarifold. It uses only:
- the contract's fields nullMeasurableSet_carrier, mult_pos, aemeasurable_mult and integrableOn_mult;
- HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature;
- the sibling child tangent_plane_ae;
- general measure-theoretic facts from Mathlib.
No result about the stronger SimonGMT Chapter04.RectifiableVarifold is used, so no bridge is needed. Its corrected lemmas are cited only for comparison:
- cutoffMass_deriv_identity (n I - t I' = -t J' - C), Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean:251;
- hasDerivAt_normalizedCutoffMass (doc: 'Corrected Simon (4.3.16) ... plus the stated mean-curvature error'), Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean:283-286;
- cutoffCancellationFactor = exp(- integral of the coefficient), Chapter04/LpCancellation.lean:162;
- cancelledCutoffMass_squeeze and exists_cancellationFactor_squeeze_of_lt (the squeeze route of step M7), Chapter04/LpCancellation.lean:400 and Chapter04/LpAnnular.lean:47.

Notation.
- mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U ∩ spt mu.
- p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp v := v - p_x v.
- B_t(z) := closedBall z t (closed) and B^o_t(z) := ball z t (open).
- omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, the volume of the closed unit ball of R^n.
- K(z,t) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z t = (t^(p-n) * integral over B_t(z) of |H|^p dmu)^(1/p), in [0, infinity].
- kappa := (p-n)/(4p) in (0, 1/4); e := exp(1).

Facts used.
(F1) [sibling child tangent_plane_ae] (a) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. (b) For mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace T_x with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x T_x (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.7) and p_x = T_x.starProjection. Hence, for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace. Then:
- p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, trace p_x = n, and <v, p_x v> = |p_x v|^2 = |v|^2 - |p_x^perp v|^2;
- for every vector a, the rank-one map v -> <a, p_x v> a has trace <a, p_x a> = |a|^2 - |p_x^perp a|^2.
By the definition of tangentProj, every p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0, so |p_x^perp v| <= |v| for all x and v.
(F1') [density at a.e. point; Simon Ch. 3, Rem. 1.8(2)] For mu-a.e. z: liminf as t -> 0+ of t^-n mu(B_t(z)) >= omega_n theta(z).
 Proof. By (F2), mu(R^(n+l) \ M) = 0, so mu-a.e. z lies in M ⊆ U and satisfies (F1)(b). Fix such z with tangent plane T, and fix eta in (0,1). Let f(w) := min{1, max{0, (1 - |w|)/eta}}. This is a compactly supported continuous function with 0 <= f <= 1, f = 1 on B_{1-eta}(0) and f = 0 off B^o_1(0).
 Let t > 0 be so small that B_t(z) ⊆ U, and let eta_{z,t}(x) := (x - z)/t (SimonGMT blowUpMap z t).
- Change of variables. eta_{z,t} is a measurable equivalence (an affine similarity of ratio 1/t), and H^n(eta_{z,t}(S)) = t^-n H^n(S) for every set S. This is translation invariance (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) combined with homothety scaling (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image); SimonGMT Chapter04 hausdorff_blowUp_image (TangentDensity.lean:31) combines the two in the same way. Hence H^n restricted to eta_{z,t}(M) is t^-n times the push-forward of H^n restricted to M (Mathlib MeasurableEquiv.restrict_map), and the integral over eta_{z,t}(M) of h dH^n equals t^-n times the integral over M of (h o eta_{z,t}) dH^n.
- Density. mu = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal o theta, where ofReal o theta is AEMeasurable (V.aemeasurable_mult) and (ofReal theta(x)).toReal = theta(x) on M. So the integral of g dmu equals the integral over M of g theta dH^n for bounded g vanishing off B_t(z) (Mathlib integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul₀). Such integrals are finite, because theta is H^n-integrable on M ∩ B_t(z) (V.integrableOn_mult); in particular the Bochner integrals of Def. 1.7 are genuine integrals.
- Since f((x - z)/t) <= the indicator of B_t(z), these two facts give
 integral over eta_{z,t}(M) of f(w) theta(z + t w) dH^n(w) = t^-n * integral over M of f((x - z)/t) theta(x) dH^n(x) = t^-n * integral of f((x - z)/t) dmu(x) <= t^-n mu(B_t(z)).
 (Only this inequality is used below.)
 By Def. 1.7 the left side tends, as t -> 0+, to theta(z) * integral over T of f dH^n >= theta(z) H^n(T ∩ B_{1-eta}(0)) = theta(z) omega_n (1-eta)^n. Here H^n on the n-plane T is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_coe_image, InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), and the closed unit n-ball has volume omega_n (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall). Letting eta -> 0 gives the claim.
(F2) [measure facts]
- mu(R^(n+l) \ M) = 0. M is H^n-null-measurable (V.nullMeasurableSet_carrier), so H^n restricted to M is carried by M (Mathlib ae_restrict_mem₀), and mu, a with-density measure of H^n restricted to M, is absolutely continuous with respect to it.
- mu(K) < infinity for every compact K ⊆ U, since mu(K) is the integral of theta over M ∩ K (V.integrableOn_mult).
- H is mu-integrable on compact subsets of U (LocallyIntegrableOn H U, part of HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature).
- If z in spt mu, then mu(B^o_eta(z)) > 0 for every eta > 0 (Mathlib Measure.mem_support_iff_forall).
- If mu(B_{t_1}(z)) < infinity and t_k decreases to t, then mu(B_{t_k}(z)) -> mu(B_t(z)): the closed balls decrease to the closed ball B_t(z), so continuity from above applies (Mathlib tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop).

Part I. The corrected monotonicity identity (M) for the contract's varifold.

M0. Setting. Let y in R^(n+l), R > 0 and Lambda > 0 with B_R(y) ⊆ U and K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda. Assume V has generalized mean curvature H in U.
 For x in R^(n+l) write rho_x := |x - y|. Put w(x) := |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2/rho_x^2 for x != y, and w(y) := 0. By (F1), 0 <= w <= 1 and w(x) rho_x^-n = |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2/|x - y|^(n+2) for x != y. By (F1)(a), x -> p_x agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel map (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk), so w agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel function. Clamp that function to [0,1] and set its value at y to 0. It stays Borel and still agrees with w mu-a.e., because w itself takes values in [0,1] and w(y) = 0. Replacing w by it changes none of the mu-integrals below, so we take w Borel with 0 <= w <= 1 and w(y) = 0.
 By (F2), m_R := mu(B_R(y)) < infinity and H is mu-integrable on B_R(y). Put ||H||_R := (lintegral over B_R(y) of |H|^p dmu)^(1/p). Then ||H||_R = R^(n/p - 1) K(y,R) <= kappa Lambda R^(n/p - 1) < infinity.
 Put g(t) := kappa Lambda R^-1 (t/R)^(-n/p) for t > 0. Since n/p < 1 and kappa p/(p-n) = 1/4, we have integral_0^t g = (Lambda/4)(t/R)^(1-n/p) <= Lambda/4 for 0 < t <= R.
 Sharp quantities, for 0 < t <= R and 0 < s <= r < R:
 I(t) := mu(B_t(y));
 C(t) := integral over B_t(y) of <x - y, H(x)> dmu(x);
 a(t) := t^-n I(t);
 E(t) := t^(-n-1) C(t);
 F_0(t) := -E(t)/(1 + a(t));
 F(t) := exp(integral_0^t F_0(u) du) = exp(- integral_0^t E(u)/(1 + a(u)) du);
 Phi(t) := F(t) a(t) + F(t) - 1;
 A(s,r) := integral over B_r(y) \ B_s(y) of |p_x^perp(x - y)|^2 |x - y|^(-n-2) dmu(x).
 F is well defined. Write C = C^+ - C^-, where C^(+/-)(t) := integral over B_t(y) of the positive/negative part of <x - y, H(x)>; these integrands are integrable on B_R(y). The functions t -> I(min{t, R}) and t -> C^(+/-)(min{t, R}) are nondecreasing on all of R (closed balls of negative radius are empty), hence Borel (Mathlib Monotone.measurable). So a, E and F_0 are Borel on (0, R]. Moreover rho_x <= t on B_t(y), so by Hoelder's inequality for lintegrals (Mathlib ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq, exponents p and p/(p-1)) |C(t)| <= t * integral over B_t(y) of |H| dmu <= t ||H||_R I(t)^(1-1/p). Hence |E(t)| <= ||H||_R t^(-n/p) a(t)^(1-1/p) <= g(t)(1 + a(t)), using a^(1-1/p) <= 1 + a. So |F_0| <= g on (0, R], which is integrable.
 For 0 < s <= r < R, the set B_r(y) \ B_s(y) = {s < rho_x <= r} has finite measure. On it the integrand of A(s,r) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable and lies in [0, s^-n]. So A(s,r) is a finite nonnegative Bochner integral. It is literally the integral in the statement, since (x - y) - p_x(x - y) = p_x^perp(x - y).

M1. Cutoffs. Let psi(v) := 1 for v <= 0, psi(v) := 1 - 3v^2 + 2v^3 for 0 <= v <= 1, and psi(v) := 0 for v >= 1. Then psi is C^1 with 0 <= psi <= 1; psi' = -6v(1-v) <= 0 on [0,1], psi' = 0 elsewhere, and |psi'| <= 3/2.
 For eps in (0,1] put phi_eps(u) := psi((u - 1)/eps). Then:
- phi_eps is C^1, nonincreasing and valued in [0,1];
- phi_eps = 1 on (-infinity, 1] and phi_eps = 0 on [1 + eps, infinity);
- phi_eps' vanishes outside (1, 1 + eps) and |phi_eps'| <= 3/(2 eps);
- for every u, phi_eps(u) tends to the indicator of (-infinity, 1] at u as eps -> 0+ (it is 1 for u <= 1, and 0 as soon as eps < u - 1 when u > 1).

M2. Radial first variation for the contract's varifold. Fix eps in (0,1] and t > 0 with (1+eps) t <= R. Let X(x) := phi_eps(rho_x/t)(x - y).
 X is C^1: it equals x - y on the open ball B^o_t(y), and on R^(n+l) \ {y} it is a composition of C^1 maps. X vanishes off B_{(1+eps)t}(y), so it has compact support and tsupport X ⊆ B_R(y) ⊆ U; DX vanishes off B^o_{(1+eps)t}(y).
 DX(y) = I, and for x != y, DX(x) v = phi_eps(rho_x/t) v + (t rho_x)^-1 phi_eps'(rho_x/t) <x - y, v> (x - y). Hence, at every x where p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection (mu-a.e. by (F1)), the trace facts of (F1) give
 div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) = n phi_eps(rho_x/t) + (rho_x/t) phi_eps'(rho_x/t)(1 - w(x)).
 At x = y both sides equal n.
 div_M X is bounded and vanishes outside B_R(y). It is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, because x -> DX(x) is continuous, x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and composition and trace are continuous. Also |<X, H>| <= R |H| times the indicator of B_R(y). So both Bochner integrals in the contract's HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature are genuine integrals. The identity integral of div_M X dmu = - integral of <X, H> dmu becomes
 (1) n I_eps(t) + integral of (rho_x/t) phi_eps'(rho_x/t)(1 - w(x)) dmu(x) = -C_eps(t),
 where I_eps(t) := integral of phi_eps(rho_x/t) dmu, J_eps(t) := integral of phi_eps(rho_x/t) w(x) dmu, and C_eps(t) := integral of phi_eps(rho_x/t) <x - y, H(x)> dmu(x).

M3. The corrected radial identity. For fixed x, the map t -> phi_eps(rho_x/t) is C^1 on (0, infinity) with derivative d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t) = (rho_x/t^2)(-phi_eps'(rho_x/t)) >= 0. This derivative vanishes unless t < rho_x < (1+eps) t.
 Fix t_0 in (0, R/(1+eps)) and choose 0 < t_1 < t_0 < t_2 < R/(1+eps). For t in (t_1, t_2):
- the integrands phi_eps(rho_x/t) and phi_eps(rho_x/t) w(x) are mu-a.e. strongly measurable, bounded by 1 and vanish off B_R(y), so they are integrable (m_R < infinity);
- their t-derivatives are bounded by 3(1+eps)/(2 eps t_1) times the indicator of B_R(y), which is integrable.
 So differentiation under the integral sign (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) shows that I_eps and J_eps are differentiable on (0, R/(1+eps)) with
 I_eps'(t) = integral of (rho_x/t^2)(-phi_eps'(rho_x/t)) dmu >= 0 and J_eps'(t) = integral of (rho_x/t^2)(-phi_eps'(rho_x/t)) w(x) dmu >= 0.
 Both derivatives are continuous in t, by dominated convergence. C_eps is continuous on (0, R/(1+eps)], by dominated convergence with majorant R |H| times the indicator of B_R(y).
 Since (rho_x/t) phi_eps'(rho_x/t) = -t d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t), identity (1) reads
 (2) n I_eps(t) - t I_eps'(t) + t J_eps'(t) = -C_eps(t).
 This is the radial identity with the plus curvature pairing; it agrees with SimonGMT cutoffMass_deriv_identity. With a_eps(t) := t^-n I_eps(t) and E_eps(t) := t^(-n-1) C_eps(t), we have a_eps' = t^(-n-1)(t I_eps' - n I_eps), so (2) gives
 (3) a_eps'(t) = t^-n J_eps'(t) + E_eps(t) for 0 < t < R/(1+eps).
 The printed 4.1 has a minus sign in front of the curvature term. With the contract's convention the sign is plus, as just computed.

M4. Hoelder bound for the coefficient. Let 0 < t <= R/(1+eps). On the support of phi_eps(rho_x/t) we have rho_x < (1+eps) t <= R. Write phi_eps = phi_eps^(1/p) phi_eps^(1-1/p). Apply Hoelder's inequality for lintegrals (Mathlib ENNReal.lintegral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq) with exponents p and p/(p-1) (p > n >= 1) to the nonnegative functions phi_eps(rho_x/t)^(1/p)|H| and phi_eps(rho_x/t)^(1-1/p). All quantities are finite, so the bound holds for the real integrals:
 |C_eps(t)| <= (1+eps) t * integral of phi_eps(rho_x/t)|H| dmu <= (1+eps) t (integral of phi_eps(rho_x/t)|H|^p dmu)^(1/p) I_eps(t)^(1-1/p) <= (1+eps) t ||H||_R I_eps(t)^(1-1/p).
 Using ||H||_R t^(-n/p) <= g(t) and a^(1-1/p) <= 1 + a for a >= 0:
 |E_eps(t)| <= (1+eps) ||H||_R t^(-n/p) a_eps(t)^(1-1/p) <= (1+eps) g(t)(1 + a_eps(t)).

M5. Corrected cancellation (integrating factor). On (0, R/(1+eps)) define F_{0,eps}(t) := -E_eps(t)/(1 + a_eps(t)). It is continuous (1 + a_eps >= 1), and |F_{0,eps}| <= (1+eps) g <= 2g, which is integrable near 0. Define
 F_eps(t) := exp(integral_0^t F_{0,eps}(u) du) = exp(- integral_0^t E_eps(u)/(1 + a_eps(u)) du).
 Then F_eps is C^1 with F_eps' = F_eps F_{0,eps}, and by (3)
 d/dt [F_eps (1 + a_eps)] = F_eps F_{0,eps}(1 + a_eps) + F_eps a_eps' = -F_eps E_eps + F_eps (t^-n J_eps' + E_eps) = F_eps t^-n J_eps'.
 The curvature terms cancel exactly because the minus sign in F_{0,eps} matches the plus pairing in (3).
 Let Phi_eps := F_eps (1 + a_eps) - 1 = F_eps a_eps + F_eps - 1. Its derivative is continuous, so the fundamental theorem of calculus gives, for 0 < s <= r < R/(1+eps),
 (4) Phi_eps(r) - Phi_eps(s) = integral_s^r F_eps(t) t^-n J_eps'(t) dt =: D_eps(s,r).
 Moreover |integral_0^t F_{0,eps}| <= (1+eps) * integral_0^t g <= (1+eps) Lambda/4. Hence e^(-(1+eps)Lambda/4) <= F_eps(t) <= e^((1+eps)Lambda/4) for 0 < t < R/(1+eps).

M6. Squeeze. Let 0 < s < r < R/(1+eps). The function (t,x) -> F_eps(t) t^-n d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t) w(x) is nonnegative and Borel: continuous in (t,x) times the Borel function w (M0). It vanishes for x outside B_R(y), so every mu-integral of it may be taken with respect to the finite measure mu restricted to B_R(y). By M3 and Tonelli for Lebesgue measure on [s, r] times that finite measure (Mathlib lintegral_lintegral_swap),
 D_eps(s,r) = integral of w(x) [integral_s^r F_eps(t) t^-n d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t) dt] dmu(x).
 Fix x != y. The factor d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t) >= 0 vanishes unless rho_x/(1+eps) < t < rho_x, where rho_x^-n <= t^-n <= (1+eps)^n rho_x^-n. Also integral_s^r d_t phi_eps(rho_x/t) dt = phi_eps(rho_x/r) - phi_eps(rho_x/s) >= 0. The point x = y contributes nothing, because w(y) = 0. With the bounds on F_eps from M5 this gives
 (5) e^(-(1+eps)Lambda/4) A_eps(s,r) <= D_eps(s,r) <= e^((1+eps)Lambda/4) (1+eps)^n A_eps(s,r),
 where A_eps(s,r) := integral over {x != y} of w(x) rho_x^-n (phi_eps(rho_x/r) - phi_eps(rho_x/s)) dmu(x) >= 0.

M7. Passage eps -> 0 to the closed-ball annular identity. Fix 0 < s < r < R and a sequence eps_k decreasing to 0 with eps_1 <= 1 and (1 + eps_1) r < R. Then (4) and (5) hold for every eps_k, and the eps_k-objects are defined on (0, r].
 (a) Pointwise limits. For 0 < t <= r and every x, phi_{eps_k}(rho_x/t) tends to the indicator of B_t(y) at x (M1), and 0 <= phi_{eps_k}(rho_x/t) <= the indicator of B_R(y). By dominated convergence (Mathlib tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), with majorants the indicator of B_R(y) and R |H| times that indicator, I_{eps_k}(t) -> I(t) = mu(B_t(y)) and C_{eps_k}(t) -> C(t). Hence a_{eps_k}(t) -> a(t), E_{eps_k}(t) -> E(t) and F_{0,eps_k}(t) -> F_0(t) for every t in (0, r].
 (b) The factor. By M0, F_0 is Borel with |F_0| <= g on (0, R], and by (a) F_{0,eps_k} -> F_0 pointwise on (0, r]. By dominated convergence in u (majorant 2g), integral_0^t F_{0,eps_k} -> integral_0^t F_0 for t in (0, r]. Hence F_{eps_k}(t) -> F(t), and Phi_{eps_k}(t) = F_{eps_k}(t)(1 + a_{eps_k}(t)) - 1 -> Phi(t) for t in {s, r}.
 (c) The annular integral. The integrand of A_{eps_k}(s,r) vanishes if rho_x <= s (both cutoff values are 1) and if rho_x >= (1 + eps_k) r (both are 0). Otherwise s < rho_x < R and the integrand lies in [0, s^-n], so s^-n times the indicator of B_R(y) is an integrable majorant.

Source: steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (Simon 2.6, inequalities (3)-(4), and the proof of 2.7: 'the set G ... includes all of spt mu ∩ B_{sigma_0/2}(0)'), with beta L replaced by an arbitrary tau >= delta^(1/(2n+2)); the parent applies this child with tau = beta L and instantiates the premise with its resolved sibling Submission.affine_approximation_lemma.

Notation. sigma_0 := delta rho; alpha := 1/(2n+2); mu := V.weight; omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0; P := p_{T_0} = (rotatedPlane q).starProjection and Q := I - P, so |Q v| = dist(v, T_0) = infDist v T_0 for every v; for any subspace T, dist(v, T) = |v - p_T v|; |A| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (|A|^2 = hsNormSq A, a norm on linear maps) and ||A|| the operator norm, ||A|| <= |A|; tilt(A) := integral over A of |p_x - P|^2 dmu; G' := spt V ∩ B_{sigma_0/2}(0); h(xi, sigma, T) := sup{dist(x - xi, T) : x in spt V ∩ B_sigma(xi)} = V.heightSup xi sigma T in [0, infinity]; K(xi, sigma) := V.scaledLpNorm H p xi sigma in [0, infinity]. The tilt hypothesis says tilt(B_sigma(xi)) <= tau^2 sigma^n for xi in G', sigma in (0, sigma_0/2].

Inputs.
(Aff) The premise AffineApproximationLemma at (n, l, p) yields C > 0; put C_A := max{C, 1} (enlarging the constant preserves both inequalities: the left side of the first one decreases and the right side of the second one increases). Thus: if 0 < delta <= 1/4, 2.3 holds, xi in spt V ∩ B_{delta rho}(0) and 0 < sigma <= 2 delta rho, there is an n-dimensional subspace T with (Aff.1) C_A^-1 (sigma^-n * integral over B_{sigma/2}(xi) of |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu)^(1/2) <= sigma^-1 h(xi, sigma, T) + K(xi, sigma) and (Aff.2) sigma^-1 h(xi, sigma, T) <= C_A delta^alpha (both in [0, infinity]).
(D) [sibling child density_monotonicity, part (ii)] There is delta_0 > 0, depending only on n, l, p, such that if 0 < delta <= delta_0 and 2.3 holds then mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2 for every y in spt V with |y| <= 3 delta rho and every 0 < s <= rho/2.
(F1) [sibling child tangent_plane_ae] x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Since ||p_x|| <= 1 for every x (p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0 by definition of tangentProj) and ||p_T|| <= 1, |p_x - p_T|^2 <= (n+l) ||p_x - p_T||^2 <= 4(n+l). Hence for every ball B with mu(B) < infinity and every subspace T, x -> |p_x - p_T|^2 is mu-integrable on B, so its Bochner integral is the genuine integral. Under 2.3, mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n < infinity, so this applies to every ball contained in B_rho(0).
(K) If B_sigma(xi) ⊆ B_rho(0) and 0 < sigma <= rho, then K(xi, sigma) <= delta: K(xi, sigma)^p = sigma^(p-n) * (integral over B_sigma(xi) of |H|^p dmu) <= (sigma/rho)^(p-n) rho^(p-n) * (integral over B_rho(0) of |H|^p dmu) = (sigma/rho)^(p-n) K(0, rho)^p <= delta^p, using p > n and 2.3.
(Extraction) In the situation of (Aff) with moreover B_sigma(xi) ⊆ B_rho(0) and delta <= 1: by (Aff.2), for every x in spt V ∩ B_sigma(xi), dist(x - xi, T) <= h(xi, sigma, T) <= C_A delta^alpha sigma (multiply (Aff.2) by sigma > 0; the supremum dominates each term). By (Aff.1), (Aff.2), (K) and delta <= delta^alpha: C_A^-1 (sigma^-n X)^(1/2) <= C_A delta^alpha + delta <= (C_A + 1) delta^alpha, where X := integral over B_{sigma/2}(xi) of |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu >= 0; squaring, X <= C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 delta^(2 alpha) sigma^n.

Proof.
1. Constants. delta_1 := min{delta_0, 1/4}; C_2 := (4 (1 + 2^n C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2)/omega_n)^(1/2); C_3 := C_A + C_2; C_5 := (2^(n+2) (1 + C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2)/omega_n)^(1/2); C_6 := C_A + C_5; C_1 := max{C_6, 4 C_3} > 0. These depend only on n, l, p.
2. Let 0 < delta <= delta_1, let 2.3 hold, and let q, tau satisfy delta^alpha <= tau and the tilt hypothesis. Since 0 < delta <= 1/4 < 1 and 0 < alpha <= 1/4, delta <= delta^alpha <= tau; so tau > 0 and delta^(2 alpha) <= tau^2. Also sigma_0 = delta rho <= rho/4, so every ball B_s(z) with |z| + s <= sigma_0 lies in B_rho(0) ⊆ U.
3. Comparison of planes. Let B be a closed ball with 0 < m <= mu(B) < infinity and let A_1, A_2 be linear maps with integral over B of |p_x - A_1|^2 dmu <= a and integral over B of |p_x - A_2|^2 dmu <= b. Then |A_1 - A_2|^2 <= 2(a + b)/m. Indeed, |.| is a norm, so |A_1 - A_2| <= |A_1 - p_x| + |p_x - A_2| and |A_1 - A_2|^2 <= 2 |p_x - A_1|^2 + 2 |p_x - A_2|^2 for every x; integrating over B (all functions integrable by (F1)) gives mu(B) |A_1 - A_2|^2 <= 2a + 2b.
4. Height bound (parent step 1). 0 in spt V by 2.3, 0 < sigma_0 <= 2 delta rho and B_{sigma_0}(0) ⊆ B_rho(0); (Aff) at (0, sigma_0) and (Extraction) give an n-plane T* with dist(x, T*) <= C_A delta^alpha sigma_0 <= C_A tau sigma_0 for every x in spt V ∩ B_{sigma_0}(0), and integral over B_{sigma_0/2}(0) of |p_x - p_{T*}|^2 <= C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2 tau^2 sigma_0^n. The tilt hypothesis at (0, sigma_0/2) (0 in G') gives tilt(B_{sigma_0/2}(0)) <= tau^2 (sigma_0/2)^n. By (D) at y = 0 and s = sigma_0/2 <= rho/2, mu(B_{sigma_0/2}(0)) >= omega_n sigma_0^n 2^-(n+1) (and it is finite). Step 3 gives |P - p_{T*}|^2 <= 2 tau^2 sigma_0^n (2^-n + C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2) 2^(n+1)/(omega_n sigma_0^n) = 4 tau^2 (1 + 2^n C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2)/omega_n = C_2^2 tau^2. Hence, for x in spt V ∩ B_{sigma_0}(0): dist(x, T_0) = |x - P x| <= |x - p_{T*} x| + |(p_{T*} - P) x| <= dist(x, T*) + ||p_{T*} - P|| |x| <= C_A tau sigma_0 + C_2 tau sigma_0 = C_3 tau sigma_0 <= C_1 tau delta rho. This proves (1); write h_0 := C_3 tau sigma_0.
5. Cone condition at small scales (parent step 2(a)). Let y, z in G' with 0 < s := |y - z| <= sigma_0/2. The tilt hypothesis at (z, s/2) (z in G', s/2 in (0, sigma_0/2]) gives tilt(B_{s/2}(z)) <= tau^2 (s/2)^n <= tau^2 s^n. Since |z| <= sigma_0/2 <= delta rho, 0 < s <= 2 delta rho and B_s(z) ⊆ B_{sigma_0}(0) ⊆ B_rho(0), (Aff) at (z, s) and (Extraction) give an n-plane T_1 with dist(x - z, T_1) <= C_A tau s for every x in spt V ∩ B_s(z), and integral over B_{s/2}(z) of |p_x - p_{T_1}|^2 <= C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2 tau^2 s^n. By (D) at z (|z| <= 3 delta rho, s/2 <= rho/2), mu(B_{s/2}(z)) >= omega_n s^n 2^-(n+1). Step 3 gives |P - p_{T_1}|^2 <= 2 tau^2 s^n (1 + C_A^2 (C_A+1)^2) 2^(n+1)/(omega_n s^n) = C_5^2 tau^2. Since y in spt V ∩ B_s(z): dist(y - z, T_0) = |Q(y - z)| = |(y - z) - P(y - z)| <= |(y - z) - p_{T_1}(y - z)| + |(p_{T_1} - P)(y - z)| <= dist(y - z, T_1) + ||p_{T_1} - P|| s <= C_A tau s + C_5 tau s = C_6 tau |y - z| <= C_1 tau |y - z|.
6. Cone condition at large scales (parent step 2(b)). If y, z in G' and s := |y - z| > sigma_0/2, then y, z in spt V ∩ B_{sigma_0}(0) and, Q being linear, step 4 gives dist(y - z, T_0) = |Q y - Q z| <= |Q y| + |Q z| = dist(y, T_0) + dist(z, T_0) <= 2 h_0 = 2 C_3 tau sigma_0 < 4 C_3 tau s <= C_1 tau |y - z|. If y = z, both sides of (2) are 0. Steps 5 and 6 prove (2). QED

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the end of step 2 and step 3 of the parent proof (Simon 2.6: 'G is contained in the graph of a Lipschitz function', (5) via the Lipschitz extension theorem Ch. 2, 1.2 applied componentwise, and the truncation (7)); the truncation is implemented by the nearest-point retraction, and the sqrt(l) loss of the componentwise extension is kept explicit.

Notation. graphPoint a b = (a, b) in R^n x R^l = R^(n+l) (first n coordinates a, last l coordinates b); horizontalPlane = R^n x {0} = {graphPoint a 0}; T_0 = q(R^n x {0}).

1. Coordinates. For w in R^(n+l) let a(w) in R^n and b(w) in R^l be the first n and the last l coordinates of q^-1 w, so q^-1 w = graphPoint (a(w)) (b(w)); a and b are linear and |a(w)|^2 + |b(w)|^2 = |q^-1 w|^2 = |w|^2 (q is a linear isometry and the Euclidean norm splits over the coordinate blocks). In particular |a(w)| <= |w|. Since q^-1 is an isometry mapping T_0 onto R^n x {0}, dist(w, T_0) = dist(q^-1 w, R^n x {0}); the point of R^n x {0} nearest to (a, b) is (a, 0), so dist(w, T_0) = |b(w)|. By linearity dist(y - z, T_0) = |b(y) - b(z)| for all y, z.
2. Lipschitz estimate on S. Let y, z in S and u := a(y) - a(z), v := b(y) - b(z). Then |v| = dist(y - z, T_0) <= eps |y - z| = eps (|u|^2 + |v|^2)^(1/2) <= eps (|u| + |v|), hence (1 - eps)|v| <= eps |u|; since 1 - eps >= 1/2, |b(y) - b(z)| <= 2 eps |a(y) - a(z)|. In particular a is injective on S: a(y) = a(z) forces b(y) = b(z), hence q^-1 y = q^-1 z and y = z.
3. The function on a(S). Define g : a(S) -> R^l by g(a(y)) := b(y) (well defined by step 2). By step 2, |g(u) - g(u')| <= 2 eps |u - u'| for u, u' in a(S), and |g(a(y))| = |b(y)| = dist(y, T_0) <= R_0 for y in S.
4. Componentwise McShane extension (Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real). If S is empty let f_1 := 0. Otherwise, for each j = 1, ..., l the component g^j is 2 eps-Lipschitz on a(S) (|g^j(u) - g^j(u')| <= |g(u) - g(u')|), so F^j(x) := inf over u in a(S) of (g^j(u) + 2 eps |x - u|) is a real-valued 2 eps-Lipschitz function on R^n with F^j = g^j on a(S). Put f_1 := (F^1, ..., F^l) : R^n -> R^l. Then |f_1(x) - f_1(x')|^2 = sum_j |F^j(x) - F^j(x')|^2 <= l (2 eps)^2 |x - x'|^2, so f_1 is (2 sqrt(l) eps)-Lipschitz on R^n, and f_1 = g on a(S).
5. Retraction. Let pi : R^l -> R^l be the nearest-point retraction onto the closed ball B_{R_0}(0) (pi(v) = v if |v| <= R_0, pi(v) = R_0 v/|v| otherwise). pi is 1-Lipschitz (nearest-point projection onto a nonempty closed convex set), |pi(v)| <= R_0, and pi(v) = v whenever |v| <= R_0. Put f := pi o f_1. Then f is (2 sqrt(l) eps)-Lipschitz on R^n, |f(x)| <= R_0 for every x, and f = g on a(S) because |g| <= R_0 there (step 3).
6. Graph property. Let y in S and x := a(y). Then |x| <= |y| (step 1) and f(x) = g(a(y)) = b(y) (step 5), so graphPoint x (f x) = graphPoint (a(y)) (b(y)) = q^-1 y and q(graphPoint x (f x)) = y. QED
proof_key_steps: Coordinates q^-1 w = (a(w), b(w)): |a|^2 + |b|^2 = |w|^2, dist(w, T_0) = |b(w)|, dist(y - z, T_0) = |b(y) - b(z)|
Cone condition with eps <= 1/2 gives |b(y) - b(z)| <= 2 eps |a(y) - a(z)| on S, so a is injective on S
g(a(y)) := b(y) is 2 eps-Lipschitz on a(S) with |g| <= R_0
Componentwise McShane extension gives a (2 sqrt(l) eps)-Lipschitz f_1 on R^n extending g
Composing with the 1-Lipschitz radial retraction onto B_{R_0}(0) gives f with |f| <= R_0 and f = g on a(S)
Every y in S equals q(graphPoint (a y) (f (a y))) with |a(y)| <= |y|

subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l >= 0 and p > n there are delta_2 > 0, eps_2 > 0 and C_2 > 0, depending only on n, l, p, such that: if U is open, V = v(M, theta) is a RectifiableVarifold n l U with generalized mean curvature H in U, 0 < delta <= delta_2 and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold, q is a linear isometry of R^(n+l) with T_0 := rotatedPlane q and P := its orthogonal projection, f : R^n -> R^l is eps-Lipschitz on R^n with 0 <= eps <= eps_2, Fhat := q(graphOver f R^n), and zeta in Fhat satisfies |zeta| <= 2 delta rho and 0 < d := dist(zeta, spt V) <= delta rho (infDist to V.support), then there is y in spt V with |y - zeta| = d, and, with s := d/2, s^n <= C_2 [ mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + integral over B_{3s}(zeta) of |p_x - P|^2 dmu(x) ], where mu = V.weight, p_x = V.tangentProj x, |.| is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm (hsNormSq), the ball measure is taken as a real number (toReal) and the integral is the Bochner integral.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof, i.e. the corrected form (10') of Simon 2.6 (9)-(10): the annulus is B_{3s} \ B_s, the monotonicity constants are the corrected ones (Lambda = 4 p delta/(p-n)), and the closest point y is produced explicitly.

Notation. (The constants delta_2, eps_2, C_2 of this lemma are its own; they are unrelated to the internal constant C_2 used in the proof of the sibling height_cone.) mu := V.weight; spt V := V.support = U ∩ spt mu; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; Q := I - P, so |Q v| = dist(v, T_0); p_x^perp v := v - p_x v; tilt(A) := integral over A of |p_x - P|^2 dmu; ||A|| <= |A| (operator norm vs Hilbert-Schmidt norm).

Inputs.
(D) [sibling child density_monotonicity] delta_0 in (0, 1/8] and C_0 >= 0 such that for 0 < delta <= delta_0 and 2.3: (i) mu(B_t(w)) <= 2 omega_n t^n for |w| <= 3 delta rho, 0 < t <= rho/2; (ii) mu(B_t(w)) >= omega_n t^n/2 for w in spt V, |w| <= 3 delta rho, 0 < t <= rho/2; (iii) for |w| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < t <= r <= rho/2: r^-n mu(B_r(w)) <= e^2 t^-n mu(B_t(w)) + C_0 delta + e^2 * (integral over B_r(w) \ B_t(w) of |p_x^perp(x - w)|^2 |x - w|^(-n-2) dmu).
(F1) [sibling child tangent_plane_ae] x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; every p_x is an orthogonal projection or 0, so ||p_x|| <= 1 and |p_x^perp v| <= |v|. Hence all integrands below are bounded on the relevant balls and mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and the balls (contained in B_rho(0)) have finite mu-measure, so every Bochner integral below is a genuine finite integral, and integrals of nonnegative functions are monotone in the domain and in the integrand.
(F2) spt mu is closed, mu(R^(n+l) \ spt mu) = 0, spt V = U ∩ spt mu, and 0 in spt V (2.3).

1. Constants. A_8 := 72 * 3^n e^2/omega_n; delta_2 := min{delta_0, 3^-n omega_n/(4 (C_0 + 1))} > 0; eps_2 := (4 A_8 omega_n 5^n)^(-1/2) > 0; C_2 := 2 A_8 > 0. Let 0 < delta <= delta_2 and the remaining hypotheses hold; note delta <= 1/8 and C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4.
2. Closest point (parent 5(a)). spt mu is closed and nonempty (0 in spt V ⊆ spt mu), so there is y in spt mu with |y - zeta| = dist(zeta, spt mu) <= dist(zeta, spt V) = d (spt V ⊆ spt mu). Then |y| <= |zeta| + d <= 3 delta rho < rho, so y in B_rho(0) ⊆ U, hence y in U ∩ spt mu = spt V and |y - zeta| >= d. Thus |y - zeta| = d = dist(zeta, spt mu): no point of spt mu lies in the open ball of radius d about zeta. Put s := d/2 > 0. As B_s(zeta) is contained in that open ball, mu(B_s(zeta)) <= mu(R^(n+l) \ spt mu) = 0. Also |zeta| <= 2 delta rho <= 3 delta rho, |y| <= 3 delta rho, s <= delta rho/2, 3s <= 3 delta rho/2 <= rho/2 and 5s <= 5 delta rho/2 <= rho/2 (delta <= 1/8), and B_{5s}(y) ⊆ B_rho(0).
3. Monotonicity at zeta (parent 5(b)). By (D)(iii) at w = zeta with t = s and r = 3s: (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= e^2 * 0 + C_0 delta + e^2 J, J := integral over B_{3s}(zeta) \ B_s(zeta) of |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 |x - zeta|^(-n-2) dmu. On that annulus |x - zeta| > s, so J <= s^(-n-2) I, where I := integral over B_{3s}(zeta) of |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 dmu (nonnegative integrand, larger domain). Hence (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= C_0 delta + e^2 s^(-n-2) I.
4. Lower bound (parent 5(c)). B_s(y) ⊆ B_{3s}(zeta) because |y - zeta| = 2s, so by (D)(ii) at y (y in spt V, |y| <= 3 delta rho, s <= rho/2): (3s)^-n mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) >= (3s)^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= 3^-n omega_n/2. Since C_0 delta <= 3^-n omega_n/4, step 3 gives 3^-n omega_n/4 <= e^2 s^(-n-2) I, i.e. s^(n+2) <= 4 * 3^n e^2 omega_n^-1 I.
5. Upper bound for I (parent 5(d)). For x in B_{3s}(zeta), p_x^perp = Q + (P - p_x), so |p_x^perp(x - zeta)|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 2 ||P - p_x||^2 |x - zeta|^2 <= 2 |Q(x - zeta)|^2 + 18 s^2 |p_x - P|^2. If x in Fhat, write x = q(graphPoint u (f u)) and zeta = q(graphPoint v (f v)); then x - zeta = q(graphPoint (u - v) 0) + q(graphPoint 0 (f u - f v)), where the first vector lies in T_0 and the second is orthogonal to T_0 (q preserves orthogonality), so |Q(x - zeta)| = |f(u) - f(v)| <= eps |u - v| <= eps |x - zeta| <= 3 eps s. If x is not in Fhat, |Q(x - zeta)| <= |x - zeta| <= 3s. Since B_{3s}(zeta) ⊆ B_{5s}(y), (D)(i) at y gives mu(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= mu(B_{5s}(y)) <= 2 omega_n 5^n s^n. Fhat is closed (f is continuous and q is a homeomorphism, so the graph and its image are closed), hence Borel, and therefore
 I <= 18 eps^2 s^2 mu(B_{3s}(zeta) ∩ Fhat) + 18 s^2 mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + 18 s^2 tilt(B_{3s}(zeta)) <= 18 s^2 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))].
6. Conclusion (parent 5(e)). Combining steps 4 and 5 and dividing by s^2 > 0: s^n <= A_8 [2 omega_n 5^n eps^2 s^n + mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))]. Since eps^2 <= eps_2^2 = 1/(4 A_8 omega_n 5^n), the first term is at most s^n/2; absorbing it gives s^n <= 2 A_8 [mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) + tilt(B_{3s}(zeta))] = C_2 [...]. Together with y from step 2 (y in spt V, |y - zeta| = d = dist(zeta, spt V)) this is the claim, with mu(B_{3s}(zeta) \ Fhat) finite (the set lies in B_rho(0)) and therefore equal to its real value. QED
